description:
Symptom (Rufus, 2026-09-26): the dashboard preview of ltp/rufus-david-collab/rufus-david-collab.ltp.yaml shows the current reality view as one flat row of cards, with no structure or edges, although the YAML has a real tree.

Data is fine (verified): the current_reality view has 38 entities and 25 relationships, all same-view with valid kinds: 18 contributes_to (a chain down to r-e-not-adopted, with loops through r-e-only-own-time), 4 challenges, 2 supersedes, 1 supports. No 'causes' links. 13 entities are unlinked (situation observations), which is expected.

Pipeline: skills/ltp-project/scripts/preview_dashboard.py (added by David in 'clean up skills', docs in skills/ltp-project/references/preview.md; see also skills/ltp-visualize/SKILL.md) converts the interchange YAML into the older dashboard model and serves or exports website/dashboard/index.html. Hypotheses to check, in order: (1) the layout only ranks nodes by certain relations (e.g. 'causes', or relations it knows from the old model) and ignores contributes_to; (2) it lays out by parent/child rather than by links; (3) it expects old-model entity types (ROLE_TYPES maps intermediate_cause -> root_cause; undesirable_effect, root_cause, evidence, observation pass through) and something about the types breaks ranking; (4) the cycles (only-own-time -> product-unclear -> ... -> only-own-time, and only-own-time <-> no-funding-applied) break a layered layout, so it falls back to a flat row. Quick test for (4): export with the two loop-closing links removed (r-rel-own-time-drives-product-unclear, r-rel-own-time-drives-no-funding) and see whether structure appears. Compare with the other views (goal tree uses parent_designation_id and necessary_for; does it render as a tree?).
